scope: Protected original VEX dword execution with independent code/address widths, explicit target features, fault/debug state and generated C

receipt.scope: Only the requested build targets and configuration; not all features or tests.
Only the requested build targets and configuration; not all features or tests.

limitations: Original CPU comparisons cover the available Intel hybrid host with BMI1/BMI2. Disabled-feature #UD and its priority are software-contract checks, not physical execution on a feature-missing processor.

Only architecturally undefined AF/PF and BEXTR SF come from an independent host probe; no defined result/flag is imported from the compared protected KVM execution. The debug fixture binds the explicit measured zero image for its fixed source/control values.

Only exact admitted VEX forms enter the executor. Reserved L/maps/selectors/mandatory prefixes and malformed extents fail admission; this does not claim hardware #UD emulation for arbitrary unadmitted bytes.
Runtime-backed protected C is new; ordinary LLVM/NeverC BMI lowering already existed. The generated i386 object lane is compile-only and runtime comparisons use Linux x64.
